infosec.summary: This article explains how access control addresses the key questions an auditor has about logs by introducing specific mechanisms: hash chains for integrity, Merkle trees with signed checkpoints for an append-only history, and trusted time anchors like RFC 3161 or OpenTimestamps. The guidance is based on established standards.

infosec.title: Fileless ELF Execution via O_TMPFILE
infosec.summary: A red-team loader chains O_TMPFILE with execveat(AT_EMPTY_PATH) to run an ELF that never gets a directory entry, allocating a real inode on /tmp with no dentry so ls, find, inotify, and fanotify never see it, then reopening the fd read-only through /proc/self/fd/ to clear ETXTBSY and executing it directly with no path string ever constructed. The technique sidesteps fileless detection built for memfd_create because it produces none of the expected artifacts: no memfd: prefix, no 00:01 device, no syscall 319, and the only residual signal is the (deleted) suffix that countless legitimate open-unlink-exec programs also generate. Defenders should stop keying fileless detection on memfd_create specifics and instead watch execveat with AT_EMPTY_PATH against anonymous /tmp/# (deleted) executables, correlating prctl(PR_SET_NAME) renames and loaders that unlink /proc/self/exe, since this combination is absent from Elastic's FENIX 15-technique matrix.

infosec.title: Wiz Red Agent Finds Its Way Into Snowflake's Internal Jira Through a Flaw in a GitHub Copilot-Assisted PR

Users of AI-assisted code generation tools should rigorously review code for introduced vulnerabilities. In this case, Copilot introduced a vulnerability by replacing a safe env + jq parsing pattern with direct string interpolation.

infosec.title: Beyond Lazarus: How North Korea Organizes Its Cyber Operations
infosec.summary: North Korea has been shown to run offensive cyber as a self-funding arm of the state, with theft revenue estimated at over a billion dollars annually feeding sanctioned weapons programs. The paper also traces the enabling layer of IT worker units, Chinese and Russian academic pipelines, and front companies such as Ryonbong and Chinyong, while cautioning that constant institutional reshuffling limits how long any DPRK org chart stays accurate.

It outperforms specialized 3D reconstruction models on benchmarks and will power future versions of Marble and other World Labs products, now entering early access with select partners.

design.title: Google Clock rolls out redesign of Timers with presets on Android
design.summary: Google Clock's redesigned Timers tab introduces one-tap presets for 1, 5, 10, and 15 minutes, along with a larger Start button and a cleaner input layout for creating custom timers. Multiple active timers now appear in a space-efficient grid instead of a scrolling list, while the countdown controls have also been reorganized. The update is rolling out via a server-side update for Google Clock version 9.1.

design.title: How Our Agents Build On-Brand Pages with design.md
design.summary: Vercel's design.md is a public file any agent can load to build on-brand pages outside the codebases where its product-design skill lives. The system pairs that guidance with a public stylesheet defining fixed classes and tokens, plus an evaluation loop that turns reviewer feedback into rules and deterministic checks. After more than 200 test runs, pages generated with design.md loaded showed 57% fewer known layout failures than those generated without it.

design.title: Good isn't good enough: beware the design middle ground
design.summary: As creative tools become more accessible, the greatest risk is not poor-quality work but settling for polished, predictable ideas that blend into an increasingly crowded middle ground. Distinctive design comes from resisting safe, incremental decisions, embracing experimentation, and making room for curiosity, intuition, and personal exploration beyond client constraints. The most memorable creative work is driven by originality and conviction rather than technical execution alone.

design.title: Reading and writing are interfaces, and AI can reduce their friction
design.summary: Criticizing all AI-assisted writing overlooks the fact that poor-quality, derivative content existed long before generative AI, and using AI does not automatically diminish the intellectual value of someone's work. The key distinction is whether AI removes incidental effort, such as editing or formatting, or replaces the critical thinking, analysis, and judgment that a task is meant to develop. Rather than focusing on whether AI was used, the more meaningful question is which parts of the thinking were delegated and which remained the responsibility of the person.

design.title: Generative AI Tools and Digital Assets for Creators
design.summary: Artlist blends premium assets with generative AI for video and image creation. Unleash your creativity with music, SFX, footage, voiceover, and AI tools.

design.title: A Daily Design Quote
design.summary: A daily design quote: every day, a thought-provoking quote from a designer the site's creator admires.

design.title: The Mac-Native Toolkit for Screenshots, Recordings, and Collaboration
design.summary: CleanShot X is a screenshot and screen recording app for Mac with a built-in annotation tool, Cloud uploading, scrolling capture, and a lot more.

design.title: Public Address rebrands Code.org as CodeAI to tackle AI literacy
design.summary: CodeAI has introduced a new brand identity to reflect its expanded focus beyond coding to AI, data science, and computational thinking, responding to the growing need for AI education in schools. Designed by Public Address, the identity deliberately avoids common AI clichés, instead presenting AI as code while combining technical elements with human-centered imagery to encourage critical thinking. The flexible, accessible system adapts to audiences ranging from students to policymakers while maintaining a consistent, future-focused visual identity.

design.title: Skogen borrows from scouting, not tech, for GridScout's identity
design.summary: Skogen created a new identity for GridScout that positions the utility technology company as “a reliable colleague on every pole,” balancing technical credibility with a warm, approachable character for everyone from field crews to executives. The redesign replaces a literal woodpecker logo with a more abstract symbol, introduces a scout-inspired visual system with badges, rugged typography, and workwear-inspired colors, and reinforces the brand through authentic photography and a Norwegian-language launch film. The cohesive identity is designed to support GridScout's growth while remaining practical, recognizable, and trusted across every touchpoint.

design.title: How to Scale Design Tokens
design.summary: Design token systems that work fine at 50 tokens often break at 500, typically because no one defined who owns changes, renames, or conflicting edits. Separating raw primitive values from semantic aliases lets a theme swap become a one-line change instead of a component-by-component hex-code audit, enforced with a simple linter rule. Treating renames as versioned, deprecation-windowed changes and generating every platform output from one source in CI, with a WCAG contrast check before shipping, keeps the system scalable.

design.title: AI Ruined Posters. This Human Designer is Fixing Them
design.summary: AI-generated posters tend to look busy, information-dense, and especially unappetizing for food imagery, prompting designer Elizabeth Martin of Ello Design Studio to redesign real AI-made posters.

design.title: OpenAI's controversial ChatGPT-6 Astra ad paints a sad vision of the future
design.summary: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra, an autonomous AI model capable of handling complex creative and technical workflows, prompting both excitement over its capabilities and concerns about safety, misuse, and its impact on creative professionals.

design.title: Turning Computational Design into Living Sculptural Skins
design.summary: 3D Beast, a New York-based architecture and computational-design practice, translates architectural systems into wearable bio-engineered structures that read as part exoskeleton, part sculpture, part prototype.

marketing.title: The big winners and losers in US website traffic over the past year
marketing.summary: Google and YouTube still dominate web traffic in the US, but AI is reshaping the landscape. ChatGPT traffic jumped 48.4% year over year to 1.09B monthly visits, while Bing fell 50.4%. Meanwhile, GA4 is losing visibility into AI-driven traffic, with “direct” traffic increasingly absorbing visits it can't attribute.

marketing.title: Streaming Is Raising Prices Faster Than Cable Ever Did
marketing.summary: Streaming prices have risen 3X faster than inflation since 2022. The 8 major services now cost around $151/month without ads or bundles, up from $90 four years ago. As subscription fatigue grows, Gen Z's “streaming cycling” trend is gaining traction. Consumers subscribe to one service at a time, then cancel and switch to another.

marketing.title: The best ads don't create desire, they borrow it
marketing.summary: The best copy doesn't create desire. It taps into wants customers already have, then connects the product to those deeper motivations. Identify the emotional driver behind the purchase, name the obstacle standing in the way, and show the customer what success looks like through a vivid, specific scenario. Rather than simply stating a benefit, make readers experience it before they buy.

marketing.title: She paid people to cancel her competitor
marketing.summary: Cursor turned a giveaway into a competitor-poaching tool by offering its $200/month plan free to customers who canceled a rival and proved it with a screenshot. Claiming meant DMing the employee running the offer from her personal account, creating a private channel for retention offers and switching feedback. A second run added a 24-hour deadline and converted even better. Customers also posted cancellation screenshots publicly, creating free marketing.

marketing.title: 🎯 Get a free AI visibility report for your brand
marketing.summary: Your buyers are using AI from first search to final decision. See what they're seeing with a free report from Evertune - the marketing platform for brand discovery in AI search. Find visibility gaps, learn which sites get cited, and generate optimized content with a purpose-built agent. Book a demo for your free report

marketing.title: New Google Ads Automated Promotions
marketing.summary: Google Ads can now automatically extract active promotions from landing pages and attach them to eligible Search and Performance Max ads. The account-level feature can surface offers such as “20% off” or “buy one get one free” without advertisers manually uploading each promotion. It applies only to eligible campaigns using location assets that do not already have manual promotions.

marketing.title: Do We Still Need Google Disavow?
marketing.summary: Google's Disavow tool is now mainly a recovery tool for sites hit with a manual action for unnatural links. Most sites don't need it after Penguin shifted spammy backlinks toward page-level devaluation. SEO efforts are better spent on useful content, UX, and earning credible links. Treat disavow as a targeted response to a confirmed manual action, not routine backlink cleanup.

marketing.title: The AI hours nobody on your marketing team is counting
marketing.summary: Every AI workflow becomes a small maintenance job once it ships. Models change, connected tools get updated, and new edge cases surface. The person who built it is often the only one who knows how to fix it, so the workflow can quickly revert to manual when they're unavailable. Teams rarely plan for this upkeep, leaving it to compete with slower, harder-to-measure work like building visibility and trust.

marketing.title: How Netflix Measures the Marketing You Cannot A/B Test
marketing.summary: Netflix uses geographic holdouts to measure channels that can't be A/B tested at the user level, including TV, OOH, and sponsorships. The approach measures incremental impact but requires careful decisions around test size, timing, media spillover, and carryover. Repeating tests builds stronger evidence, while campaigns without historical data require different methodologies. The challenge is getting leadership to protect test windows and accept the tradeoff between media delivery and measurement certainty.

marketing.title: Marketing resume tips
marketing.summary: 8 tips to tailor your marketing resume to the job you want.

marketing.title: Why Nvidia is buying Hugging Face
marketing.summary: Nvidia plans to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9B to strengthen the open-source AI ecosystem around its chips.

marketing.title: AI chatbots talked 57.5% of AI users out of buying
marketing.summary: AI chatbots now influence purchases in both directions, persuading 57.5% of AI users to buy and 57.5% to walk away.

crypto.title: DBS/Citi complete first weekend cross-border USD payment
crypto.summary: DBS and Citi completed a Singapore-to-US USD payment over a weekend using tokenized deposits via Swift's Digital Ledger, taking minutes versus up to two business days for traditional cross-border transfers. The move removes weekend/time-zone delays for institutions operating across jurisdictions. Citi joined Swift's 24/7 tokenized payments pilot in July and is also part of a group of major US banks building a separate tokenized deposit network through The Clearing House, targeting a 2027 launch.

crypto.title: Hanwha builds tokenized securities platform on Avalanche
crypto.summary: South Korean brokerage Hanwha Investment & Securities reportedly built a tokenized securities platform (started in 2025 with FairSquare Lab) running on Avalanche and Hyperledger Besu, ahead of South Korea's securities tokenization law taking effect in February. Regulators plan a phased rollout starting with private money market funds, bonds, and unlisted stocks, eventually expanding to public securities and stablecoin settlement rails. Hanwha is also Securitize's largest shareholder (9.6% stake) and separately invested $22.3M in Canton Network operator Digital Asset.

crypto.title: RowDAS (EIP-8371): Distributed Blob Reconstruction, measured
crypto.summary: EIP-8371 (RowDAS) proposes adding 128 row-based subnets to Ethereum's PeerDAS architecture to eliminate the redundant blob reconstruction work that every qualifying node performs on its own. Under the present design, an estimated 2,000+ nodes each spend 5.18 seconds of CPU per slot reconstructing 32 blobs. RowDAS distributes that load, cutting per-reconstructor time to 40 milliseconds and network-wide CPU from 10,400 to 81 seconds at 32-blob scale. The design uses a two-dimensional cell matrix where column subnets retain custody authority while row subnets pool reconstruction, allowing ordinary nodes to reach the erasure-coding threshold without high-stake infrastructure. A Prysm prototype with real KZG cryptography exists, though mainnet-scale testing is pending, and a duty-sharded fallback variant preserves 91% of CPU savings for staged rollout before the full row layer activates.

crypto.title: Wyoming Puts Its Stablecoin Reserves Onchain With Under $1 Million Outstanding
crypto.summary: Wyoming's Stable Token Commission adopted Chainlink Proof of Reserve on September 2 as the exclusive verification layer for the Frontier Stable Token (FRNT), routing reserve and supply balances audited by The Network Firm to an onchain feed. FRNT's outstanding supply of 967,948 tokens priced at $0.9988 each represents 0.2% of the 508.7 million token base case the Commission projected to state lawmakers in December, with just $160 in 24-hour trading volume occurring on Kraken. The Proof of Reserve Secure Mint component, which would programmatically block minting without verified reserve backing, remains unimplemented. The integration is Wyoming's second Chainlink partnership in a month, following an August 18 migration from LayerZero to Chainlink CCIP that the Commission attributed to security review concerns and LayerZero's disclosure practices.

crypto.title: The Shape of Ethereum: A Six-Year Study of Topological Anomalies
crypto.summary: Researchers applied Topological Data Analysis to six years of Ethereum transaction data (2020-2025), segmenting daily activity into four layers and using Wasserstein distance to quantify structural changes between consecutive days. The pipeline flagged 86 anomalous periods, with 85% corresponding to documented events including Black Thursday liquidation cascades, DeFi repositioning two days after the Ukraine invasion, and post-Bybit hack fund dispersal across bridges. Unsupervised change-point detection identified six structural breaks tied to identifiable catalysts, and preliminary results show TDA features improve 7-day ETH volatility forecasts beyond GARCH baselines. Layer composition shifted from governance-dominated anomalies in 2024 (11 of 16 events) toward plain ETH transfers in 2025, though the absence of a labeled ground-truth dataset limits validation of which events structurally alter chain topology.

crypto.title: Who Killed the Cryptoanarchist?
crypto.summary: Cryptoanarchy, the movement centered on data privacy, permissionless systems, and trust minimization, retreated during the 2020-2022 bull cycle as crypto companies prioritized institutional capital and mainstream UX over ideological principles. Each value the movement abandoned has since been validated by AI-era behavior: users now hide camera rolls from Instagram and stockpile Mac Minis to host open-source models, while businesses treat every networked system as an attack surface for misaligned agents. Most original cryptoanarchists have either exited the space or reframed their work for institutional audiences, leaving the movement hollowed out precisely when broader society began internalizing its core concerns. A revival is possible under new banners, with AI-driven threat models replacing the 2008 financial crisis as the animating fear.

crypto.title: Coldcard exploiter moves 45% of Wave 3 stolen funds
crypto.summary: The attacker behind the Coldcard hardware wallet exploit (a 2021 firmware bug that weakened seed randomness) has moved 45% of Wave 3 stolen bitcoin, per Galaxy Research, swapping some to ETH via THORChain, then running funds through CoinJoin. About $7.8M has been spent so far, moving stolen vaults largest-first. 82% of all exploited funds remain in attacker-controlled addresses. Total identified losses across all waves now stand around 1,806 BTC (~$143.9M), with Galaxy flagging a possible Wave 4.

crypto.title: Mapping onchain BTC credit solutions
crypto.summary: Surveys four approaches to unlocking bitcoin-backed credit without a fully taxable wrap: Anchorage's Atlas (a legal collateral-agent structure mainly for CeFi lenders, thin smart-contract layer), Komainu (a Nomura/Ledger/CoinShares JV using a legal "Notice of Exclusive Control" and Liquid Network settlement), Babylon Labs (fully non-custodial, BTC never leaves its own chain via Taproot dual-spending paths), and Concrete's AssetCX (BitGo custody plus a real 1:1 ERC-20 synthetic usable as DeFi collateral). Concrete is the most "DeFi-native" since it's the only one built around an actual onchain token rather than a legal wrapper.

crypto.title: MENA crypto volume hits $350B
crypto.summary: Middle East/North Africa on-chain transaction volume grew from ~$100B in 2022 to ~$350B in 2025-2026.

crypto.title: Banks becoming DeFi's real competitors
crypto.summary: Recent US bank charter approvals signal banks are about to gain the same programmability and 24/7 settlement DeFi protocols have relied on as differentiators.

crypto.title: Satoshi-era Bitcoin wakes after 16 years of dormancy as 600 BTC moves
crypto.summary: 600 BTC (~$48 million) transferred from 12 addresses dormant for over 16 years, each holding proceeds from a single block reward mined in March 2010 at the original 50 BTC subsidy.

it.title: Sophos brings OpenAI models to vulnerability prioritization
it.summary: Sophos is developing Exploit Path Verification to assess whether attackers can actually exploit vulnerabilities given an organization's network access, privileges, patches, and security controls. The capability will use OpenAI cyber models with analyst review, but availability has not been announced.

it.title: Claude Fable 5.1 on AWS comes with new data controls
it.summary: Claude Fable 5.1 is available through Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS, with prompts and outputs subject to retention for up to 30 days and potential safety review by Amazon personnel. Planned Enterprise Frontier Safeguards will let eligible customers keep monitoring data in cloud infrastructure they control.

it.title: A decade of software infrastructure
it.summary: The next decade will be defined by software infrastructure as AI turns everything into infrastructure. This post outlines six megatrends, including AI-rebuilt development lifecycles, infrastructure re-architected for agents, and APIs replacing apps. Agent-driven buying and early-stage machine-learning infrastructure are predicted to expand opportunities for infrastructure startups.

it.title: Have the frontier labs mixed up AI safety and security?
it.summary: Frontier AI labs confuse probabilistic AI safety with deterministic security, treating prompt-injection defenses as largely solved despite high failure rates. False positives, weak containment like proxy and firewall gaps, and reliance on detection over containment enabled the failures.

it.title: Run cloud agents on machines you manage
it.summary: Cursor now lets cloud agents run on your own infrastructure, while Cursor still handles the agent loop, inference, and orchestration. Self-hosted workers can scale dynamically across AWS, Vercel, Modal, Cloudflare, Macs, etc., which gives teams direct access to internal systems, custom hardware, and existing build environments.

it.title: OpenShift adds a unified secrets management console
it.summary: Red Hat's new console plug-in brings certificate and external secrets resources into one interface, helping administrators investigate expiration warnings and failed dependencies. It is available as an administrator-only technology preview for OpenShift 4.22.

it.title: FINOS introduces portable records for AI-assisted work
it.summary: The konspekt project proposes an open format for preserving project decisions, artifacts, and source provenance across AI tools. Records live in plain files and require human acceptance, creating an audit trail independent of any model provider or chat platform.

it.title: Explaining 3PL
it.summary: A third-party logistics provider holds a brand's inventory and handles picking, packing, shipping, and returns while the brand keeps product and customer ownership. This explainer details its rate-card pricing, EDI and API integrations, and cut-off times, arguing that warehouse location and performance directly set delivery dates in Shopping ads and marketplace badges like Prime. It also notes rising fee and mandate disputes, including Amazon surcharges and conflicting accounts of TikTok Shop's shipping mandate.

it.title: Amazon Linux 2027 enters public preview
it.summary: The preview includes kernel 7.1+, SELinux enforcement by default, updated development tools, and AWS Neuron driver support.

it.title: Does Concentration Risk Matter In AI?
it.summary: Heavy revenue concentration among AI labs and across the AI stack does not necessarily give large customers leverage - vulnerability is accessed by layer.

it.title: AI spending outpaces proof
it.summary: Enterprises are experimenting with budgets and model routing while struggling to measure returns.
